questions.stem: What is the result of rotating the figure 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis?
questions.solution: When rotating an object 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis, the x-coordinates change to -y and the y-coordinates remain the same. The correct rotation is shown in option A.
questions.explanation: Option A correctly shows the figure rotated as described. Option B does not rotate enough, Option C rotates too much, and Option D rotates around the wrong axis (x-axis instead of y-axis).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Rotating around the x-axis instead of the y-axis.

questions.stem: A cube is rotated 90 degrees about the y-axis. Which face will now be facing directly upward?
questions.solution: Rotating a cube 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis will cause the top face to move upward and become the front face. The correct answer is option C.
questions.explanation: Option A remains in its original position, Option B moves to the back, and Option D moves to the bottom. Only Option C faces upward after rotation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Confusing clockwise with counterclockwise rotation.

questions.stem: A right rectangular prism is rotated 90 degrees about the y-axis. Which pair of edges will now form a right angle?
questions.solution: Rotating the prism 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis causes edge FG to align with edge AB, forming a right angle. The correct answer is option D.
questions.explanation: Options A, B, and C do not form right angles after rotation. Only Option D forms a right angle as a result of the rotation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not considering how the edges change relative to each other during rotation.

questions.stem: A triangle with vertices at (1, 2), (3, 4), and (5, 6) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis. What are the new coordinates of the vertex (5, 6)?
questions.solution: Rotating the triangle about the y-axis results in a change of x-coordinates to negative values while the y-coordinate remains the same. The new coordinates for (5, 6) are (-5, 6).
questions.explanation: Option A and C have incorrect signs, Option D has both coordinates negated, which is not correct for a rotation about the y-axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Forgetting to change only the x-coordinate sign.

questions.stem: A circle with center (3, 4) and radius 2 is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis. What are the new coordinates of the center?
questions.solution: Rotating the circle about the y-axis causes the x-coordinate to change sign while the y-coordinate remains the same. The new center is (-3, 4).
questions.explanation: Option A and B have incorrect signs on the x-coordinate, Option D has both coordinates negated, which is not correct for a rotation about the y-axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not accounting for the change in x-coordinate sign.

questions.stem: A parallelogram with vertices at (1, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), and (7, 8) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis. Which vertex will be located at the point (6, 5)?
questions.solution: Rotating the parallelogram about the y-axis causes vertex (7, 8) to be located at point (6, 5). The correct answer is option D.
questions.explanation: Option A moves to (2, 1), Option B moves to (4, 3), and Option C remains in its original position. Only Option D ends up at the specified point after rotation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not recognizing how the vertices change positions during rotation.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon with vertices on the Cartesian plane is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the y-axis. Which vertex will now be at the origin?
questions.solution: Rotating the hexagon about the y-axis causes vertex (0, 1) to be located at the origin. The correct answer is option B.
questions.explanation: Option A moves to (0, -1), Option C remains in its original position, and Option D moves to (-1, 0). Only Option B ends up at the origin after rotation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not considering how the hexagon's vertices change during rotation.
